chunks: And as for what was narrated - Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah from Aban from Abd al-Rahman al-Basri who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a Christian man whose wife chose Islam, and her residence (dar al-hijrah) [is]: that she is in the abode of Islam and is not expelled from it, and her conjugal right (bud') is in the hand of her Christian husband, and she does not inherit him, nor does he inherit her.' This report and the one we presented earlier from Umayy al-Sayrafi are both narrated in agreement with the general public (Ahl al-Sunnah) on what they narrate from the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), and their narrators are also the narrators of the general public. And this ruling is to be taken as being due to precaution (taqiyyah) and is not taken as definitive if it contradicts all other reports.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)

ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance and marital status ruling for a Muslim woman married to a Christian man?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam Ali (AS) establishes that in a mixed-faith marriage, the Muslim wife retains her domicile within the 'abode of Islam' while her conjugal bond (buz') remains with her Christian husband, resulting in no mutual inheritance. Al-Tusi contextualizes this by noting its alignment with Sunni tradition and suggests it may be a case of *taqiyyah* or specific circumstance rather than a universal, independent legal principle, distinguishing it from other narrations. This highlights the nuanced Shia approach to interfaith family law, prioritizing the stability of the marital bond while maintaining distinct inheritance boundaries.
